samples.summary: Disposal revocation is built on the mutator DENYLIST that `read-only.ts` documents as fails-open (issue #989), now load-bearing for a second condition

The new revocation path inherits that known failure mode: a mutating `EditorAPI` member added tomorrow will keep writing through a disposed editor (the exact stale-write hazard this change exists to close), and nothing in CI detects the omission. The store side is covered by `revocableDocStore`; only the api surface is left on the pattern the repo already decided against.

finding.summary: Indent/outdent/list-toggle logic is duplicated three times and only one copy got the undo unit, so the same user action now answers differently — and the toolbar copy keeps the #1045 data-loss shape
finding.evidence: `handleIndent`/`handleOutdent` in `text-editor.ts:2815,2840` were wrapped in `withUndoUnit`, but the byte-for-byte equivalent logic in `editor.ts:3632 indent()` / `3656 outdent()` / `3612 toggleList()` (same `MAX_LIST_LEVEL = 8`, `INDENT_STEP = 36`, same `forEachBlockInSelection` loop) and the third copy in `text-box-editor.ts:1140,1163` were not. Result: Tab / Cmd+] over a 100-item list is one undo unit, while the *toolbar's* indent / bullet buttons over the same selection still issue one `doc.update()` per block — 100 units against Yorkie's 50-entry cap, i.e. exactly the unrecoverable-tail failure the issue is about, reachable through a different button for the same action. The new docs text (docs-collaboration.md, "Not yet every multi-write action") admits this and defers it to #1048, but the divergence is created by this change: before it, all copies behaved identically. The change also had to fix the inline-style path twice (`editor.ts` `applyStyleImpl` and `text-editor.ts` `applyStyleToSelection`), which is the same duplication showing up as double maintenance.

verdict.reason: The finding's core premise — that only the keyboard copy got the undo unit while the toolbar copies still issue one doc.update per block — is false in this tree. editor.ts's EditorAPI toggleList (3629), indent (3652) and outdent (3680) each wrap their forEachBlockInSelection write loop in doc.batch(...), with docStore.snapshot() outside and layout/paint after; the third copy in text-box-editor.ts (toggleList 1121, indent 1146, outdent 1172) is batched identically. TextEditor.withUndoUnit is literally `this.doc.batch(fn)` plus deferred-render bookkeeping (text-editor.ts:3894-3905), and Doc.batch delegates to store.batch, which YorkieDocStore runs as one doc.update (document.ts:127-153). So Tab/Cmd+] and the toolbar indent/bullet buttons produce the same single undo unit; the claimed 100-units-against-the-50-entry-cap divergence does not exist, and no user-visible "same action answers differently" behavior is reachable. The cited docs text says the opposite of the finding's reading: docs-collaboration.md:314-327 states the toolbar paths are covered one by one and names applyBlockStyle/toggleList/indent/outdent/cell writers; lines 336-344 defer to #1048 only the remaining code duplication, explicitly because routing EditorAPI through TextEditor is not behaviour-preserving (TextEditor.toggleList acts on the caret block, EditorAPI on the selection). The residual triplication is real but behaviourally identical across copies and documented in the canonical subsystem doc, so it does not carry the "duplicated logic that will now diverge and give two answers" cost the major grade rests on.
